chunk_map.heading: # Read the session before you fix it (title slide, no lede)

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 1's 'The session' (line 5) and 'This session' (line 9) resolve via the module-arc opener carve-out: `learn-from-the-test.md` §Start here states 'You sent off an un-packaged session' immediately before including this lecture (grep confirmed at line 22 of that file), so 'the session' is prior context by module include-order, not a slide-1 orphan. 'The un-packaged send-off' (line 7) resolves the same way, and is itself an established beat from M4 (`run-the-first-experiment.md` line 23, 'Send off the task un-packaged'), so it also clears rule 3. 'The read' (line 7, 'what the read finds') ties back to the chunk's own header verb ('Read the session' / 'Diagnose') — same chunk, no forward pointer. Harm check: the rule exists so a reader can't be handed a pronoun with no candidate; here every candidate is named in the module's own signposting one slide before this file opens, so the harm (an unresolvable referent) is not present.
No 'the opening lecture said' / 'that story' style cross-file callback anywhere in the two-chunk body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'The un-packaged send-off was the test' (line 7) points at M4's send-off exercise. Confirmed live in `curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/run-the-first-experiment.md` line 23 ('Send off the task un-packaged in the same Claude Code session') and line 39 (`[Exercise: Prep the run, fill the gaps](exercises/walk-and-send-off.md)`) — the beat exists in the current module set, not a stranded reference.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal instructional device in this file — it states a diagnostic stance, it doesn't stage a predict-then-check beat.
Chunk 1 carries three self-carrying bullets plus a kicker sentence, not a single wait-state fragment. Chunk 0 is a normal bare title slide.

Header 'Diagnose first, fix later' is supported by all three bullets (stopped/finished/data → diagnose it; the bolded maxim restating the header; the test→learn→encode arc placing diagnosis before any fix) — nothing in the chunk contradicts the header's claim.

Checked all sub-items against the two-chunk body: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction; the three-sentence test→learn→encode mapping (line 7) uses distinct concrete content per leg (send-off / this lecture / the encode step), not a repeated-refrain anaphora triple; no self-grading superlatives; no numbers present, so no number+retraction pairs; no abstraction-noun stacks; the verb list 'edit the prompt, add a constraint, reach for the next tool' (line 6) names three distinct concrete engineer actions, no empty leg.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No repo/maintainer vocabulary (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, Connections-as-proper-noun) anywhere in the body. 'This module' is ordinary curriculum vocabulary used throughout the corpus, not internal dialect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 0 has zero bold. Chunk 1 has exactly one bolded element, '**Diagnose first. Fix later.**' (line 6) — a 4-word coined mantra functioning as the slide's named handle (it restates the chunk's own header), followed by unbolded explanatory prose, not a bolded whole descriptive sentence. Within the ≤1-per-slide budget and the ≲5-word handle cap; not the pre-2026-07-09 every-bullet-bolded pattern the rule bans (only 1 of 3 bullets is bolded).
